newsitem.title: UK: Coffee use seen rising by 15 mln bags in 10 years.
newsitem.headline: Coffee use seen rising by 15 mln bags in 10 years.

text.p: World coffee consumption could rise by 15 million bags over the next decade but new markets are needed for any appreciable growth, according to a report published by German statistician F.O. Licht on Friday.

The report, written by William Struning, managing director of Washington D.C-based firm Commodity Decision Analysts, said it was unlikely, although not impossible, for North America or West Europe to carry world demand to significantly higher levels.
This was because both regions appeared to have reached maturity in their coffee product-life cycles, it said.
World consumption is estimated at 100 million bags in 1996/97.
In the United States, the immediate consumption outlook may be dim but it is not bleak, it said.
The overall market could absorb as much as 25 million bags of coffee per year, however, that is unlikely especially in the near future, it added.
In Western Europe, the potential for growth is far from uniform, the report added.
The Scandinavian countries are already consuming at high level per capita rates. Further gains, although possible, seem unlikely.
Disappearance in almost all countries of the central tier countries of Western Europe was down from recent peaks, especially in Austria, Belgium and Germany.
For the near-term, the potential Western European market seems confined to about 40 million bags.
Overall, increasing consumption in the region will be more feasible in the south than in the north.
In Asia and Oceania (excluding China), there is more potential for coffee consumption in producing rather than in consuming countries.
Among new markets, eastern Europe could raise coffee consumption to 10 million bags from around six million currently, while in China the ultimate potential for coffee is great.
But only a fraction of that potential seems realiseable in the near future. "One approach would be to set a short-term goal of, say, two million bags," the report added.
Coffee use in producing countries grew by 19 percent over the past seven years to an anticipated 25 million bags in 1997/98 coffee year, the report said.

"...Conditions for encouraging further growth seem to exist," it said, adding that 30 million bags would be a realisable potential over the next decade. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
